title: First coordinate Gaussian score bound
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set, let $c=(c_j)_{j\in I}\in\mathbb R^I$, and let $v>0$. Equip $\mathbb R^I$ with the product Gaussian measure whose coordinate at $j$ has mean $c_j$ and variance parameter $v$. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and satisfies $|f(z)|\le1$ for every $z$, then for each $i\in I$ the function $z\mapsto ((z_i-c_i)/v)f(z)$ is integrable, and its integral has absolute value at most $1+1/v$.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real, hence $v>0$
replaced: Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $|f|\le1$ and $i\in I$, then $z\mapsto((z_i-c_i)/v)f(z)$ is $\mu_{c,v}$-integrable and $|\int((z_i-c_i)/v)f(z)\,d\mu_{c,v}(z)|\le1+1/v$.
